about: The outcome of one failed operator-surface call (exit not 0), per runner action and the product path it calls. A row matches when its code equals the answer's code and its action and path equal the call's or are "*". A matching unknown row decides unknown. Otherwise a matching refused row decides refused when it has no message_contains or the answer's message contains that text exactly. Every other failed answer, with or without a row, is unknown, for a read of the state to decide. A refused_effect row is a refusal with a documented effect: the product refused, and a PAGE line (effect.cite, docs/<page>.md:<line>) states what the refused call changed anyway (effect.part, effect.to); its completion carries that effect. An effect stated only in code never makes a row refused_effect: the row stays unknown and is listed in page_gaps with the code line, the page read and why it does not state the effect. Refused means nothing changed, so a refused row needs a citation that the product states that. Unknown rows record a code kept unknown on purpose, with the reason. Codes of ops chunk are its JSON error codes; codes of ops workspace are exit codes; codes of v3ctl are the master's gRPC code names, and v3ctl (packs/v3block/v3ctl/main.go, built inside the product checkout) keeps a compiled copy of its rows that a test keeps equal to them. Every match on product text (an effect's *_contains, a row's message_contains) is listed in phrases with its source line and the product test that pins it, or null; each is a product gap until the product treats it as an interface. An effect that relies on a phrase no product test pins is refused at load, unless the row is marked pending_pin: it then decodes unknown, keeps its effect, and is listed in product_gaps; setting the phrase's pinned_by makes it count with no other edit. A pin is direct (the test runs the matched command) or indirect (through another call); an indirect pin counts only when the phrase comes from code both paths share (shared_source).

the cut writes before its commit loses: with changed data it begins its session on HEAD (a conditional HEAD update) and uploads the chunks and the session's root, then the commit finds HEAD moved past its base; it discards what it staged, aborts the session (another HEAD write) and the snapshot withdraws its name. HEAD's generation and the file listing change. The operator page tells the operator to retry it with the same name (docs/operator-guide.md:220-225): the declared snapshot reruns it, each attempt its own operation

a volume at layout.MaxSnapshots refuses a new name before the cut opens a session, under the volume's snapshot lock (the only path that adds a name), so the refusal writes nothing: no snapshot, no cut, HEAD as it was (the page; TestChunkSnapshotPastTheLimitIsRefusedWithHEADUnchanged)

only the reservation's own refusal changes nothing: the publisher refuses while a lease is live before calling persist, the master answers FailedPrecondition for that sentinel alone, the CLI wraps it as ErrNotAdmitted and answers not_admitted with err.Error() as the message. Reserve runs first. The same code after the reservation committed (RunMarkDeleting) carries no such text, and a rerun after a commit replays the reservation, so it never carries it. The product has no separate code for this refusal; the sentinel is its error text, so not_admitted without it is unknown
